newsitem.title: USA: Time Warner chief Levin's son found dead. [corrected 22:10 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Time Warner chief Levin's son found dead. [corrected 22:10 gmt]

text.p: The badly decomposed body of Jonathan Levin, son of Gerald Levin, chairman of media giant Time Warner Inc., was found in a Manhattan apartment on Monday night, police said.
Levin's body was bound and gagged though there were no visible stab or gunshot wounds, a police spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
She said Levin's body was discovered in his Columbus Avenue apartment at about 10:30 p.m. EDT on Monday (0230 GMT Tuesday).
"We are shocked and saddened by the death of Jonathan Levin," Time Warner President Richard Parsons said on Tuesday.
Levin, a 31-year-old (corrects from 34-year-old) English teacher at Taft High School in the Bronx, did not turn up for work on Monday, school officials said.
A police spokeswoman said other teachers who lived in the same building had called police after one of them, who had a key to Levin's apartment, found the body on Monday night.
A dog was found locked in Levin's bedroom, she said.
Gerald Levin took over as chairman of Time Warner in 1992, replacing Nicholas Nicholas. Time Warner was formed by the 1989 merger of Time and Warner communications.
